newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian Airlines to suspend some payments.
newsitem.headline: Canadian Airlines to suspend some payments.

text.p: Canadian Airlines Corp said on Monday its Canadian Airlines International Ltd unit planned to suspend payments to lenders and aircraft lessors of about C$170 million of C$265 million due over the next six months.
The amounts owed would be repaid on a basis to be negotiated, Canadian Air said. The normal payment schedule would resume in May 1997.

"The debt deferral provides a short-term financial bridge for the airline until the longer-term benefits of the operational restructuring plan begin to take effect," said president Kevin Benson in a statement.

"We believe that our lenders and aircraft lessors will be supportive, to the extent that six out of our seven employee groups at this point are ready to contribute to make the company profitable, as are three governments and our partner AMR Corp," Benson added.

The deferral affects 70 banks, trading and leasing companies. It does not impact suppliers who provide goods and services necessary for the operation of the airline. Canadian Airlines will have meetings with the lenders and lessors during the next two weeks, with a goal of having an agreement in principle with most parties by early 1997.
